title: Air traffic disruption readiness eyed
summary: Sen. Raffy Tulfo has filed Senate Resolution 784 to probe the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP)’s readiness to ensure the security, reliability and continuity of air traffic…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo has filed Senate Resolution 784 to probe the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP)’s readiness to ensure the security, reliability and continuity of air traffic services in the event of a major communications outage.

The move follows a Nov. 13 incident in the United States that forced the Federal Aviation Administration to declare a nationwide ground stop, temporarily preventing aircraft from taking off for about four hours.
Tulfo recalled the Philippines had experienced a major technical failure on Jan. 1, 2023, involving the CAAP’s Communications, Navigation, and Surveillance/Air Traffic Management system.
The incident disrupted hundreds of flight operations and affected around 65,000 passengers.

As chairman of the Senate committee on public services, Tulfo coordinated with Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon and CAAP chief of aerodrome and air navigation safety oversight Capt. Bryan Balagtas to discuss the issue.

The incident in the US should serve as a wake-up call for the government to strengthen the CAAP’s aviation infrastructure and ensure the reliability of systems essential to the safe, orderly and efficient movement of aircraft, Tulfo stressed.
Tulfo said that it is imperative for the Department of Information and Communications Technology to present its preparedness plan if such wide-scale digital disruptions occur.
